independence.note: Continued only from own 04:02 checkpoint and public primary sources.

checked_sources.source: Rohan Deb, Mohammad Ghavamzadeh, Arindam Banerjee, Conservative Contextual Bandits: Beyond Linear Representations, arXiv:2412.06165
checked_sources.result: Primary-verified a sequential exploration method with an explicit baseline fallback at every round. C-SquareCB/C-FastCB first propose an exploratory action, test a safety condition, and play the known baseline instead when the condition cannot be certified. The safety requirement is uniform over time: cumulative loss through every t must remain at most (1+alpha) times baseline cumulative loss. For neural online regression, the paper gives regret O(sqrt(K T log T)+K log(T)/alpha) for C-SquareCB and a first-order bound O(sqrt(K L* log(L*) log T)+K log T+K log(T)/alpha) for C-FastCB, while satisfying the performance constraint with high probability.

checked_sources.source: Abbas Kazerouni, Mohammad Ghavamzadeh, Yasin Abbasi-Yadkori, Benjamin Van Roy, Conservative Contextual Linear Bandits, arXiv:1611.06426
checked_sources.result: Primary-verified the earlier linear conservative-bandit principle: maintain performance above a fixed percentage of a known baseline uniformly over time, while regret decomposes into the usual learning term plus a conservatism penalty that does not grow with the horizon under the stated assumptions. This supports the baseline-shadow/fallback principle independently of the newer nonlinear construction.

candidates_new.mechanism: Keep a known baseline policy as a live shadow throughout exploration. Before executing a proposed exploratory action, certify that cumulative performance remains inside a baseline-relative safety budget; if certification fails, execute the baseline action instead. This makes fallback an explicit online action rather than a post-hoc rollback.
candidates_new.primary_source: Deb, Ghavamzadeh & Banerjee, arXiv:2412.06165; Kazerouni et al., arXiv:1611.06426
candidates_new.quantitative_evidence: The nonlinear CCB paper enforces, with high probability, cumulative loss <= (1+alpha) times baseline cumulative loss for every t. With neural online regression it derives O(sqrt(K T log T)+K log(T)/alpha) regret for C-SquareCB and a first-order O(sqrt(K L* log(L*) log T)+K log T+K log(T)/alpha) bound for C-FastCB. The safety price enters as additive terms scaling with 1/alpha rather than changing the leading horizon dependence.
candidates_new.operational_observable: Maintain baseline cumulative loss, exploratory-policy cumulative loss, current safety slack/budget, proposed action confidence, fallback count, alpha, regret versus optimal policy, and cost attributable to conservative fallback. Every exploratory action should have a pre-action safety-certificate receipt.
candidates_new.scope: Contextual bandit sequential decisions under realizability/online-regression assumptions and a baseline with known expected cost; safety is cumulative baseline-relative performance, not arbitrary scientific correctness.
candidates_new.failure_conditions: Requires a trustworthy baseline and enough knowledge to bound or know its expected performance. Very small alpha forces frequent fallback and increases the K/alpha conservatism cost. A weak baseline prevents catastrophic degradation relative to that baseline but does not guarantee absolute high utility. Model misspecification outside the realizability/confidence assumptions can invalidate certification.
candidates_new.transfer_hypothesis: For research automation, every risky new scheduler/evaluator/research policy can run behind a current-production shadow. Adopt experimental decisions only when a cumulative utility/safety budget can be certified; otherwise execute the existing baseline path. This gives a direct target-only/current-policy fallback primitive that complements r16's pathwise validity controller.
candidates_new.confidence: high for source-domain baseline-fallback principle; medium-high for research-loop transfer

evidence_updates.update: r19 supplies the explicit baseline-relative utility fallback that r16 lacks. The two primitives are complementary: r16 preserves pathwise validity accounting via an unprojected controller and boundary actions; r19 preserves cumulative utility relative to a known baseline by certifying each exploratory action and falling back when needed. No primary source found here proves the exact composition of both guarantees in one algorithm.

deferred_or_negative_evidence.lead: A baseline fallback makes exploration free of opportunity cost.
deferred_or_negative_evidence.evidence: False. The conservative contextual-bandit regret bounds include additive terms scaling as K/alpha (and log factors), so stronger baseline protection increases the conservatism price.
deferred_or_negative_evidence.reason: Tune the safety slack explicitly and measure fallback cost rather than treating safety as free.

deferred_or_negative_evidence.lead: Baseline-relative safety is equivalent to absolute safety or scientific correctness.
deferred_or_negative_evidence.evidence: False. The guarantee is relative to the specified baseline's cumulative performance and depends on model/confidence assumptions.
deferred_or_negative_evidence.reason: A bad or mismeasured baseline can be safely matched while still being objectively poor.

frontier: Find a single primary method that composes an anytime/pathwise validity-debt controller like r16 with an explicit baseline/current-policy utility fallback like r19, ideally under partial/bandit feedback.
Find sequential transfer/admission where the baseline is target-only learning rather than a fixed known policy and prove no-negative-transfer or bounded excess regret uniformly over time.
Find online repeated-round proposal-shift conformal certification with estimated density ratios and finite-sample validity after adaptive prior experiments.
Extract empirical stopping-time tail and overhead curves for exponential-tail best-arm wrappers and analogous restart wrappers in distributed/asynchronous search.
Find finite-budget covariance-aware ranking/selection under genuinely heavy-tailed paired/common-random-number observations with robust estimators and exact PCS guarantees.

actions_taken_instead_of_stopping: Continued the exact validity+utility frontier after the 04:02 checkpoint rather than stopping at report readiness.
Searched conservative sequential decision methods and found a direct live baseline fallback with uniform-over-time performance protection and sublinear regret.
Separated baseline-relative safety from absolute scientific correctness and recorded the 1/alpha conservatism cost.
Kept the frontier nonempty because no single source yet composes r16 pathwise validity with r19 baseline-relative utility protection under the same limited-feedback process.

exact_next_action: Search for conservative/safe bandit or online-learning algorithms that maintain both a pathwise calibration/constraint debt and a baseline-relative reward/loss floor under limited feedback. Prefer a theorem with uniform-over-time target-only/current-policy fallback. If absent, examine safe policy improvement/off-policy evaluation and e-process-based constrained decisions for a composable bridge.
